claims.text: Nanoscale, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi thin films or nanoribbons have magnetocaloric response and hysteresis controlled primarily by surface/interface strain and local magnetic inhomogeneities.
Surface/interface strain and local magnetic inhomogeneities disrupt the long-range collective magnetostructural transition observed in bulk FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys.
Spatial variations in magnetic anisotropy and pinning suppress the cooperative magnetocaloric response and broaden the transition.
Broadening of the magnetic transition increases hysteresis.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi nanoscale films or patterned nanoribbons possess significant intrinsic residual stress and local chemical or structural disorder.
Low-temperature post-deposition annealing can relieve residual strain in the FeMnNiGeSi samples.
Low-temperature post-deposition annealing can promote short-range chemical ordering without causing grain coarsening or changing sample dimensions.
Residual interfacial strain and defect density produce a broad distribution of local magnetic anisotropy and magnetic order.
Nanoscale dimensions enhance the influence of surface/interface stresses and defects.
Surface/interface stresses and defects reduce magnetic-domain homogeneity and smear the field-induced magnetic transition underpinning the magnetocaloric effect.
Annealing-induced reduction of defects and local strain will sharpen the magnetic transition.
Annealing-induced reduction of defects and local strain will reduce hysteresis and improve magnetocaloric-cycle efficiency.
Relative to the as-deposited baseline, annealed samples will exhibit a larger magnetocaloric temperature change under the same low applied field.
The magnetocaloric response may improve by approximately 20–40% after annealing.
Annealed samples will exhibit narrower M-T loops and a sharper, more cooperative magnetic transition than as-deposited samples.
As-deposited samples have high defect density and spatial magnetic inhomogeneity that produce a broadened transition, diminished magnetocaloric response, and enhanced cycle hysteresis.
The proposed behavior applies particularly to films or ribbons with a thickness or width below 100 nm.
The proposed behavior applies under sub-100 mT fields near the alloy's magnetic transition temperature.
Heat-transfer limitations restrict the magnetic-cooling cycle frequency under the stated operating conditions.
